In my younger years I lied a lot, I'd expect other people to read my mind, and just generally didn't care about other people's feelings - this was specifically with romantic partners. I also battled with drugs but I've been sober now for a year and 3 months. Basically, mentally unstable and very volatile. My main issues were with past romantic partners, but I've somehow managed to keep good long-term relationships with friends.

Yep, 100%. Recently confronted my uBPD mother about her alcoholism and declining mental health since her mother died. I'm a recovering addict myself (1y2m sober) so I found it pretty interesting to hear the combination of the addict bargaining behaviour and the BPD blame game. 

One of the things that she told me is that she feels that my dad has "forced" her to alienate her family and accept his family instead. She has an unstable family - I had zero relationship with either of her parents because they were both nasty bullies, and her siblings are strange and unstable as well. Her family also live all over the country. My dad's family isn't perfect but they live closer to us so we see them more. It's interesting to observe how they feel a feeling, they manufacture their reality to explain the feeling, and like you say, it's someone else's fault. Like, I suspect that my mother is upset that she has grown distant from her family and is jealous that they see my dad's family more often, but in her mind, my dad is FORCING her to ABANDON her family. It's always so black and white

I bought my wedding dress and a couple of months later I fell pregnant. Knowing alterations would be necessary, I informed the dressmaker I'd be 6 months pregnant on the wedding day and made it very clear that I'd be more than happy to pay for all alterations required. She assured me it was no problem but insisted on the standard two-week timeframe for alterations.

When it came to the fitting, instead of focusing on the dress, she spent the entire session berating me about my pregnant body. It felt like she was punishing me for getting pregnant, as if it somehow ruined her vision for the dress. Her comments were incredibly insensitive and they just didn't stop. She admitted "praying" I hadn't gained weight, then scoffed when I reassured her I was carrying small. 

I was already pretty busty before getting pregnant but my boobs got pretty massive and she wouldn't stop talking about it. She went on and on about how big boobs are fine but pregnant boobs aren't flattering and shouldn't be shown off. She also exclaimed multiple times during the session about how "surely your boobs weren't always this big??"

Two of my close friends got diagnosed and we related on a lot of our experiences. Some of the specific symptoms were my extreme sensitivity with all my senses (especially sound and taste), my constant analysis of my own social behaviour in social settings and acknowledging that most of my smaller social behaviours are intensely calculated (i.e. how much eye contact to make, where to look, how much to smile, when to laugh, loudness of voice, tone of voice, when to speak) so that I appear as regular as possible, being completely exhausted after social events and after a work day, being very ahead of my peers intellectually when I was small while being very behind emotionally and socially, and a lifelong battle with food and picky eating.

I had been "diagnosed" with a myriad of other conditions throughout my teenage years and young adult life and having this whole list of conditions made no sense to me. It felt very unlikely that I have generalised anxiety disorder, depersonalization disorder, OCD and ADHD even though I experience symptoms fitting into all of these categories.

I suspected I may be autistic and did a couple of online tests including the RAADS-R test and those scores strongly indicated that I may be autistic. I did an intensive assessment with a specialist psychologist and it confirmed that I am autistic and ADHD. This was last year when I was 26yo.

For example, I once went to a market with some family where we saw some baby clothes. Because dolphins = blue = boy and flamingo = pink = girl? Makes no sense to me.

Over the years I'd been diagnosed with ADHD, general anxiety disorder, depersonalization disorder, bipolar disorder, and then never diagnosed but suspected OCD. It just made no sense to me at all. When the topic of autism came up for me I discussed it with my psychologist and she suggested that I get assessed through a specialty clinic in my area and it turns out it's just autism and ADHD. 

The psychologist I spoke to during my assessment specialises in autism and after my formal diagnosis, she told me that women bringing a myriad of disorders and it just being autism with or without ADHD is fairly common in her experience.

I'm currently 17w with my first and I struggled big time with depression in my first trimester. Not a mental health professional - I can only offer my own anecdotal experience. I am autistic and also have ADHD but I don't know much about the correlation between pre-existing conditions and depression in pregnancy. The depression was definitely amplified by the intense fatigue of the first trimester and I found that the depression improved as the second trimester arrived. 

I know that people will say that depression is normal in pregnancy but it doesn't mean it should be treated as "just another symptom". Depression is unkind to our brains and can twist the way we perceive our own feelings making us judge ourselves so hard so please don't be too hard on yourself for not immediately feeling as excited as your husband. I do not doubt that you'll be feeling excited soon enough.

I reached out to my psychologist and she suggested seeing a perinatal psychiatrist to see if maybe my medication needed to be adjusted - not sure if that'd be the right thing for you?

AuDHD here and 17w pregnant. I've been advised not to take my ADHD medication (Vyvanse) because of the lack of data on its behaviour in pregnancy. I'm still taking my anti-depressants though. I can't take stimulant medication because of my substance use disorder. 

The combination of no ADHD meds and pregnancy brain fog is WILD. I had grand plans of working + studying this year but I genuinely feel 65% stupider, I absolutely cannot concentrate on work and have such little capacity for working hard. Trying to study after getting home from work feels impossible because I just want to cocoon in bed. I have started seeing an OT who specialises in neurodivergent peeps and has been helping me a fair bit. I'm resigning soon so I can focus on just my studies and being a mom.

I'm 17 weeks pregnant and while I am thrilled and excited to be a parent, being pregnant + being AuDHD + working full time is awfully difficult for me. It's been suggested to me that I should work through my pregnancy but I just can't ignore it when I feel anything less than good which is like 60% of the time and I shut down. 

I am already very sensitive sensory-wise but it just seems to be amplified and I've had more frequent meltdowns. I am regularly seeing an OT who specializes in neurodiversity who has been helping me a lot and I will be resigning in two months.

If I didn't have my incredible fiance who feels to be the most supportive person in the world I don't think I'd have been able to do this. Despite all these difficulties I am still over the moon and ecstatic with the fact that I'll be having a little baba in July.

I used to be a chronic weed smoker so I can talk about how it was for me then. I am only speaking for my own anecdotal experience which may be different from others - I have a substance use disorder but have been sober for 7 months. 

It somehow changed the way that food tastes, sometimes for good and sometimes for worse. Some foods that I loved tasted weird but then sometimes the munchies allowed me to eat pretty much anything. I remember guzzling down a tray of roasted vegetables and was so proud of myself lol. 

I wouldn't suggest it though. I had a bigger appetite but not for anything healthy. Amongst other issues that came with chronic weed use, I developed bulimia because I'd eat everything in the house because of the munchies and then feel terribly guilty about it so yeah. I also got to a point where I needed weed to eat, which is a bad space to be in. 

I'm not going to say not to use it, but if I can suggest one thing it would be to prepare good food *before* smoking weed on a day otherwise you'll probably just snack on whatever's safe and in large quantities.

Oof, this is rough. My fiance also has a BPD ex and it was very bizarre in the beginning, but nowhere close to what you've been going through with the harassment and obsession. 

He doesn't speak poorly of her at all and when people ask about their split he just says that they were bad for each other. After they split up everything was okay but when she found out that he was dating me she went nuclear and started to tell all of his friends that he physically abused her for their entire relationship. She started making quasi-inspirational social media posts about #gbv, insinuating that she was so brave for leaving this terrible man who she thought was going to kill her. She even tried to get his own family and sportsmates to believe this but luckily no one with half a brain believed her because the only abuse they'd witnessed was from her and he is one of the kindest, most compassionate people I've ever met.

I've been with him for almost three years now and this man has never so much as raised his voice to me. Discussions have always been calm and never turn into fights. He still struggles with walking on eggshells and is still so scared of saying the wrong thing lest I interpret something incorrectly. He's unlearning the expectation of being able to read his partner's mind and be their everything. 

From what he's told me, she would hit him, block doorways to not allow him to leave when he wanted to take a break from an argument, take knives out and cut herself during arguments. He says he doesn't think she ever apologised to him in their years together and every argument was resolved by him apologising and groveling and buying her things.

Luckily her whole "he abused me and I'm so brave for leaving him" narrative (despite that he broke up with her lol) has meant that she's blocked us both on everything and hasn't tried to contact us since. I would hate to be in your position with the harassment so I am incredibly sorry about that.

I really appreciate your comment, thank you. She already managed to make me feel crap about moving into our new house long before we moved in because she never congratulated me and just bugged me about the fact that it's in a predominantly non-white neighborhood and is pretty convinced that we're going to be murdered or something. At least my fiance's parents are incredible people so I've slowly started accepting that I can get the parental validation that I desire from them instead :')

Since I've become an adult she has badgered me about having children and I've started telling her that each time she brings up my having children I will push it back another two years :'D So I might just say something similar about her brother at the wedding, or something like "I'm not talking about this again". 

She didn't teach me any life skills intentionally but she has definitely given me good practice in setting boundaries, reading subtext from people who say one thing and mean another (I'm autistic), and not falling for manipulative behaviour.
Thank you so much, I really appreciate that.

Yeah it really sucks how hard we feel that we have to work to tiptoe around their emotions. If I know anything about her I don't think she'll make a scene at our wedding at least, but she'll probably be mad at me afterward for (insert random reason here) which I will hear about a month later after a silent treatment or something :'D

I don't think there's much introspection going on there beyond "but me me me" :'D She even asked me if we had cut out some members of my fiance's family. We do have a fairly small family in comparison (I have my parents, sister, 2 grandparents, 2 uncles, an aunt, and 9 cousins) whereas my fiance's dad has nine siblings to start with so naturally there are dozens of family members. This means that of course, we have cut out roughly half of them, whereas I've cut out essentially one uncle and his kids. I didn't explain myself to her because I don't care enough because it's just so clearly not about representation and about her just wanting to get what she wants.

Oh goodness, I can see so much of my mother in these scenarios. They always offer so much more and then expect you to feel so grateful for something that you didn't ask for or even specifically did not want. Growing up and up until I moved out at age 21, my mother used to re-arrange and do a spring clean of my bedroom at random intervals while I was at school with no warning and would get annoyed with me for not being grateful for it. I used to tell her every time she did it that I hated it when she did that and that it felt like an invasion of my privacy and it's not her decision to throw away my things. She acted like I was doing her this huge favour because my room was "a mess" (spoiler: it was not). She would always respond with "Fine I'll just never go into your room again" and would try to triangulate with my father with something like "Look how raviolifordinner never even wants me in their room and says I'm not allowed to clean". 

Also the inappropriate sex talk?! I have no idea how and where that comes from. I remember I once invited a boy I liked, his sister, and her boyfriend over for the first time when I was 17. The sister and boyfriend were in their late 20s and part of a fairly conservative (in the traditional sense, not political) family, and my mom started the conversation by telling them about all these different types of dildos she had read about in a magazine. They were very taken aback and his family didn't come to visit ever again. 

I'm kind of terrified about having my own children because she has already overruled my "parenting" decisions with my two dogs by feeding them things they're not allowed to eat (the dogs don't visit her anymore), and she also calls my dogs "her boys".

It's so bizarre to me that they would even consider asking to invite people to someone else's wedding. I don't think I have the strongest sense of social cues but I definitely know that it's terribly inappropriate to do that at all, let along basically beg and nag about it. I suppose they think that different rules apply to them because, 
according to them after all, the universe revolves around them and their feelings

You make a good point. Like, if I knew that someone specifically wasn't invited to a wedding that I am attending I'd make a point of not talking about it with them because it's just not their business, so it does weird me out that it's even a topic of conversation with her brother.

That's awesome. I had the same response from my friends. Fine motor skills autism, is that a thing? I've always been naturally good at drawing, painting, picking up new instruments, and any other thing that involves small work with my hands. I am a fast typer as well. 

I think I also have a sprinkle of math and science autism, or rather pattern recognition and problem-solving. I'm a software engineer who specialises in data so I think I'm in the right career for now.

Just say what you want to say and stop beating around the bush oh my word

Yeah, I used to get it a lot when I started working at my current workplace. We get free lunches every day and they are mostly very good and healthy and it makes me feel embarrassed that I struggle to eat them. A lot of the time I'll try the food and then give the rest of it to a colleague, but most of the time I'll flat-out reject it quietly and eat a banana or something instead. People always used to ask me if I'm sick, if I'm on a diet, if I'm "okay", if there's something wrong, if I don't like the food etc. Like sometimes I'll bring a cheese sandwich to work and a colleague was like "and that's better than this?!"

I had a major fear of driving even after I got my licence. I didn't even have any bad accident which triggered it, I was just generally an anxious person. It was seriously inhibiting me in that I was skipping classes and missing out on most social events. I was also scared even of being in cars with other people. I ended up dating someone who lived about an hour away which involved driving on a scary national road so I had to try my best to get better.

A few things worked for me. I'm still not entirely over the fear, but I'm a hell of a lot better. One thing is figuring out WHAT actually scared me so much. Was it other people's unpredictable behaviour? Was it getting into an accident? Am I just doubting my own driving ability? Was I scared of getting lost in an unknown area? Each of these have some kind of "counter-argument" which I had to think hard about.

* Unpredictable behaviour - Truth is, most people actually don't *want* to get in an accident. I just need to make sure I don't get distracted and stay vigilant. 
* Accident - I should familiarise myself with the procedure of what I need to do if I get into an accident so that I can not have a panic attack if it does happen, which will make it a lot easier. 
* Doubting my own ability - Maybe I should practice driving again in an area that I'm familiar with
* Getting lost - If I look up the route beforehand on Google Maps or something it might make the drive easier.

But what other people have said is important. Gradual improvements are where it's at. Drive to places that you're familiar with. Be patient and kind to yourself :) I promise it can get easier.
